numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With an infinite weight (weights=[np.inf, 1]) on exact antiparallel vectors, Rotation.align_vectors([[0, 1, 0], [-1, 0, 0]], [[0, -1, 0], [-1, 0, 0]], weights=[np.inf, 1])[0].as_rotvec() returns array([0., 0., 0.]), i.e. a 0 degree rotation, because a perfect 180 degree rotation gives cross = [0, 0, 0] and is cast to identity. Near 180 degrees there is also a pointing error of 2e-6 in the test case; the test assertion output shows ACTUAL array(3.1) versus DESIRED array(3.141593).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: array([3.14159265, 0., 0.]) as the rotation vector (equivalently a rotation magnitude of pi), matching the finite-weight result weights=[1e6, 1]; near 180 degrees the pointing error should drop from 2e-6 to 5e-9 and match the non-exact code path to 1e-11.
trigger_conditions: weights contains np.inf (infinite weight) for an exactly antiparallel vector pair
rotation angle exactly or nearly 180 degrees so that cross product is zero or theta is near pi
small-angle Taylor branch used instead of flip handling when theta is near pi

input_output_examples.input: Rotation.align_vectors(a, b, weights=[np.inf, 1]) with a=[[0, 1, 0], [-1, 0, 0]], b=[[0, -1, 0], [-1, 0, 0]], test asserts np.isclose(R.magnitude(), np.pi, atol=1e-12)

oracle_clues: AssertionError from assert_allclose with rtol=1e-07, atol=0 showing ACTUAL array(3.1) vs DESIRED array(3.141593)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Near pi radians (180 degrees) rotation angle; the flip branch applies when abs(np.pi - theta) < tolerance, and the small-angle branch applies when abs(theta) < tolerance
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: 1e-3 rad for the small-angle/flip threshold (tolerance = 1e-3, '# tolerance for small angle approximation (rad)'); test uses atol=1e-12 for magnitude and apply checks
category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is an infinite weight (weights=[np.inf, 1]) on an exactly antiparallel vector pair; the buggy output is array([0., 0., 0.]) instead of array([3.14159265, 0., 0.]), while weights=[1e6, 1] gives the correct result
Exact 180 degree rotation gives cross = [0, 0, 0], so cross_norm == 0 and r = cross is cast to a 0 degree rotation; this is where the zero cross product enters
Correct handling in the fix: when cross_norm == 0, an arbitrary orthogonal axis is set (i = np.argmin(np.abs(a_pri[0])); r[i-1], r[i-2] = a_pri[0][i-2], -a_pri[0][i-1]); otherwise r = cross

Flip step: R_flip = Rotation.from_rotvec(r / np.linalg.norm(r) * np.pi), then theta = np.pi - theta and cross = -cross, and the small-angle rotation is applied on top with R_pri = Rotation.from_rotvec(r) * R_flip
Near-180 instability: pointing error of 2e-6 reduced to 5e
reproduction_risks: Infinite weight (np.inf) is the trigger; the passages do not state the exact float dtype
Passages do not state the precision (float64 or otherwise) explicitly
Exact equality of np.pi and atan2 pi limit is discussed but not confirmed
